title: Runtime re-homing: health-gated VPC data-plane upgrade orchestrator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: implement a deterministic, zero-downtime upgrade orchestrator for VPC/private data-plane runtime upgrades that uses a health-gated "rehoming" pattern to move tenant workloads away from nodes being upgraded, validate warm-state correctness (KV cache, session affinity), and provide automated rollback within defined SLOs. This ticket covers the orchestration operator, Terraform hooks for IaC rollout policies, and a small set of in-cluster health probes and telemetry gates required by the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can rehome traffic for a single tenant from an old runtime instance to a new instance with no 5xxs and <50ms p95 additional latency for 95% of requests during handoff
Automatic KV-cache priming step completes before traffic cutover and is validated by application-level checks (cache-hits and key-consistency probe)

If any health gate fails (startup readiness, cache-consistency, model-variant handshake, connection-saturation) the orchestrator aborts cutover for that tenant and marks an automated rollback triggered state
Terraform module exposes rollouts as an apply-time plan: wave size, max-concurrent-rehomes, prewarm_timeout_seconds, and fallback_policy; these inputs must be documented and tested in e2e harness

Operator exposes a retriable failover path with a safe-rollback window (configurable, default 10 minutes) and emits structured audit logs for each handoff (tenant, from-instance, to-instance, start_ts, end_ts, reason, outcome)
Runbook created and linked: step-by-step human-override for abort, manual rehome, and emergency failback
End-to-end test in staging that performs a full cluster upgrade using operator and validates no user-visible errors across ten synthetic tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Preparation: add Terraform flags to private deployment module (allow_rehome, prewarm_seconds, health_gate_thresholds). Roll out module change to staging IaC only
Phase 1 - Operator deploy in passive mode: operator validates cluster topology, registers instances and tenants, but does not perform handoffs

Phase 2 - Health probe standardization: deploy lightweight in-process probes (cache-consistency, model-handshake, qps-saturation, forwarding-latency). Operator reads these probe endpoints for gating decisions
Phase 3 - Canary rehoming: pick a low-traffic tenant, perform prewarm (KV sync), reroute traffic test for 10m, monitor telemetry; abort if >1% error delta or p95 latency regression >200ms
Phase 4 - Wave-based rollout: progressive waves defined by Terraform module input (default wave size 10 tenants), operator executes waves and respects max-concurrent-rehomes

Phase 5 - Fallback & rollback: if gate violations exceed configured thresholds in two consecutive waves, operator triggers automated rollback for waves completed within the last X minutes and quarantines affected instances
Phase 6 - Post-upgrade verification: run synthetic-eval prompt set on a sample of tenants, reconcile embedding/kv integrity, collect and store traces for 72h
failure_modes: Cold-start latency spike due to missing KV prewarm -> mitigated via prewarm step and prewarm_timeout_seconds
State drift where rehomed instance returns different outputs for identical prompts (model-variant mismatch) -> gate on model-handshake probe and manifest verification
Network flakiness causing partial connectivity -> operator enforces quorum of health checks from at least 3 independent probes before signoff
Operator churn (operator pod restart during handoff) -> idempotent handoff protocol with lease tokens and case reconciliation
High concurrency causing downstream overload -> operator respects max-concurrent-rehomes and backpressure from per-instance connection counters
telemetry_and_alerts: Metrics to emit: tenant_handoff_started, tenant_handoff_succeeded, tenant_handoff_failed, handoff_duration_seconds, kv_prewarm_time_seconds, cache_consistency_ratio
Dashboards: per-wave success rate, p95 latency delta (pre/post handoff), error-rate delta, per-tenant health history
SLO gates: if handoff_failure_rate > 1% over sliding 30m window -> auto-pause rollouts and create incident ticket
Audit logs: structured JSON events sent to audit-elk with tags: operator_version, terraform_plan_id, release_tag
Alerts: PagerDuty on high-severity rollback (>3 waves aborted) and on any customer-facing 5xx spike post-rollout
implementation_notes: Design decision: use a rehome-first approach (move traffic away from node) instead of drain-last to guarantee isolation of upgrade activity
We will implement prewarm via a sidecar that can sync KV prefixes using an efficient snapshot+delta protocol; sidecar exposes /internal/cache_status
Operator will implement a two-phase commit: PREPARE (prewarm + probes), COMMIT (traffic switch), COMPLETE (decommission old bindings). COMMIT is reversible for the rollback window
Terraform changes limited to module input parameters and lifecycle hooks; operator controlled actions are applied post-terraform via an operator-run job referencing the module's plan id
Security: operator's actions must be signed and recorded; use existing KMS-backed signing service for operator-issued audit events
